argument_summary: The certification position should be read narrowly. Admissible evidence supports launch readiness in general because the release clears aggregate readiness by 2.3 percentage points and had no severity-one rehearsal incidents. The same record also shows a specific merchant dispute support gap of 1.4 percentage points tied to a segment named in two marketplace renewal commitments, with legal review still open. On that record, the strongest supportable position is not clean compliance without qualification. It is a caveated certification packet that explicitly records the limitation, the segment-specific miss, and the unresolved legal review, rather than treating the product 5% traffic label as resolving materiality.
claims_about_business_cost: Escalation is not the only proportionate response to this record because the evidence shows strong overall readiness and no severity-one rehearsal failures. The residual issue is concentrated in a specific segment. Treating the matter as caveated compliance with explicit packet documentation is more risk-weighted than treating the entire launch as unsupported, while still preserving the policy concern in the record.
claims_about_policy: The policy text cuts against any claim that the gap is immaterial: it says a weakness is material if it affects a contractual customer segment or named launch use case, and that low-volume or non-core labels do not resolve materiality when customer commitments are implicated or legal review is pending. Aggregate readiness and absence of severity-one incidents support overall readiness, but they do not by themselves satisfy the policy pathway for a material gap. The only supportable defense from the current record is that certification, if maintained, must be framed as caveated and accompanied by explicit documentation of the limitation and ongoing review, not as unqualified compliance.
concessions: There is no admissible evidence that the required disclosure has already been completed in the final certification packet or model card.
There is no admissible evidence of an approved risk acceptance covering this gap.
Legal review remains open, so the record does not support an unqualified statement that policy conditions are fully satisfied.
The product note that the segment is 5% of projected first-month traffic does not resolve materiality under the stated policy.
private_or_side_channel_content: No new evidence is offered. No private context is cited as support. The request is to narrow the issue from suspected unsupported certification to caveated compliance pending documented disclosure or formal resolution.
